findings.issue: Real heteronym: verb "close" is /kloʊz/, while adjective "close" is /kloʊs/. The meaning lists both, but only the verb pronunciation is given; the example is also the verb.
IPA has an extra /r/ after the r-colored vowel (/kɝr-/); standard American is /ˈkɝɪdʒ/. The phonetic field also begins with a space.
findings.context: He showed great courage in the race.

findings.issue: Sense-dependent: furniture "drawer" is /drɔr/, but the person senses listed (开票人；起草者；酒馆侍) are /ˈdrɔːər/. IPA and example cover only the furniture sense.
findings.context: She kept the keys in the top drawer.

findings.issue: Same extra /r/ as courage: standard American is /ɪnˈkɝɪdʒ/, not /ɪnˈkɝrɪdʒ/.
First vowel is transcribed /i/ but should be /ɪ/: /ˈɪŋɡlənd/.
Stress is misplaced and two primary stresses are marked; standard stress is on "-pe-": /ˌjʊrəˈpiːən/.
Uses /ʊ/ in "Feb-ru-" and marks two primary stresses; standard is /ˈfɛbruˌɛri/ (also /ˈfɛbjuˌɛri/).
Phonetic field is empty; no pronunciation is supplied.

result.notes: No audio was supplied; review is text-only. I treated the widespread use of "e" for /eɪ/ and omitted length marks (date, day, eight, famous, etc.) as a systematic notation convention rather than individual errors. Ordinary US/UK variants (either, comfortable, crayon, direct, clothes reduced /kloʊz/) were not marked. "excuse" is a real noun/verb heteronym, but the entry is noun-only and internally consistent. Non-pronunciation data notes: classroom repeats the same IPA twice; dialogue's example uses the variant spelling "dialog". No acronym/code-spelling issues found.
